data.narrative:
Orbital Inc., a seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Euwyn Poon, operates within a 13-company peer universe spanning 5 public equities (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX and Rocket Lab.

The valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression. Using total capital raised as a proxy baseline of $16 million, a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $40 million. The peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Space & Aerospace sector—14 same-sector peers exist, but none met the three-datapoint minimum for narrow filtering. Public-comp anchoring was inapplicable because Orbital's revenue is not on file; the sector median P/S of 27.4x across 6 public tickers cannot be deployed without revenue disclosure.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $34–46 million, with a median of $40 million. This range reflects a ±15% confidence band around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the accuracy of the raised-capital proxy (actual amount undisclosed) and the appropriateness of a 2.5x multiplier for this specific company's risk profile and market conditions. A more granular assessment would require either disclosed revenue or access to tighter private-peer comparables at seed stage.
